climate_pressure: Cyclone Ditwah flooding and landslides during the November 2025-January 2026 emergency.
documented_impact: Displacement and damaged access routes increased dependence on temporary shelters and disrupted assistance.
fcv_mediator: Crowding, insufficient lighting and privacy, shared sanitation and gaps in accessible protection services raised exposure to harm.
possible_consequence: Heightened gender-based violence risk reported by UNFPA; no measured cyclone-attributable incidence.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing inequalities, household resources and service quality also influence protection risk.
Agency reporting is not an incident-based causal evaluation.
uncertainty: This is a source-stated post-disaster protection-risk mechanism, not proof of increased violence incidence, anthropogenic attribution of the cyclone, or a national FCV classification.
resilience_factors: Accessible shelters, privacy, lighting, sanitation and functioning protection referrals can address the reported risk factors; effectiveness is not evaluated.
compact_statement: Post-Ditwah shelter conditions and protection-service gaps heightened GBV risk; incidence changes were not measured.
